**HARD PRECONDITION OF PR4 (external ruling rev 11, issue #297): PR4 MUST NOT consume [FAIL-SHA] until the modify-shaped-denial suppression AND its frozen fixture have landed.**

**The binding, stated so it cannot be missed by whoever builds PR4.** The A10 fix (PR3c) widened the reverter-exemption liveness guard from ADDED paths to ADDED-or-MODIFIED paths. That closes a live governance fail-open, and it has a measured cost: a LEGITIMATE modify-shaped tip-most cleanup reverter now loses its exemption and emits [FAIL-SHA] -- the auto-revert signal -- even though its entire contribution was REMOVAL. A consumer acting on that signal would revert the cleanup and RESURRECT the payload it removed. That is the precise harm design §15.5 names when it requires "never revert the intermediate legit reverter".

**Why the fix shipped anyway (rev 11, staged C, by elimination).** A10 was a LIVE fail-open on the integration branch, reproducible today. The false-[FAIL-SHA] harm-window does not open until PR4 exists to consume the signal. Holding the live hole hostage to machinery guarding a not-yet-existing consumer is the fix-first pattern rev 9 already eliminated: its premise ("keep the branch clean of an intermediate") is unavailable while a hole is live. So the shape was staged -- fix now, guard bound to the consumer it protects against.

**What must land before PR4 consumes [FAIL-SHA]:**
1. THE FINDER writes a mechanism-blind fixture pinning the property "a legitimate modify-shaped cleanup reverter is REPORTED but NEVER carries [FAIL-SHA]", proven RED against the post-PR3c state. C-b requires the fixture before any suppression patch regardless.
2. THE PATCHER then implements the suppression: the exemption site must distinguish "denied because a touched path is live at the tip" from an ordinary un-exempted tree-keyed failure, and thread that distinction to the emission block, so the merge still reports [FAIL] (never a silent PASS) but emits no auto-revert signal.

**Failure direction if this binding is ignored.** PR4 reverting a cleanup reverter is not a noisy false positive -- it is a silent governance REGRESSION that puts an ungoverned payload back on the tree, automatically, with the audit's own signal as justification. The [FAIL] line alone is safe; the [FAIL-SHA] line is not.

**Provenance:** ruled at #297 rev 11 after the patcher's measured ## FORK (options implemented, run against the frozen set, and reverted). Option A unbound was ELIMINATED precisely because it would ship this named harm into a channel a planned consumer will read.
